traceability.evidence: Rule implementation: - src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts implements deep requirement validation: - Reads story files and extracts requirement IDs via regex /REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+/g (loadAndCacheRequirements) satisfying REQ-DEEP-PARSE and REQ-DEEP-FORMAT. - Caches parsed requirements per resolved story path in a Map, only reading each file once per lint run (REQ-DEEP-CACHE). - Validates @req lines via validateReqLine -> resolveStoryAndRequirements -> checkRequirementExists, reporting messageId "reqMissing" when a requirement is absent (REQ-DEEP-MATCH, REQ-DEEP-ERROR). - Validates @supports lines via parseImplementsLine + validateImplementsLine, checking each listed REQ-ID against the target story file (integration with 010.2 multi-story support). - Validates story paths (both for @story and @supports) with validateAndResolveStoryPath: rejects ".." and absolute paths, and ensures resolved paths stay under cwd, reporting messageId "invalidPath" (path safety and integration with file validation concerns). - Uses try/catch around fs.readFileSync; on any file read error it stores an empty Set for that path so linting continues gracefully, treating requirements as missing rather than crashing (graceful error handling for malformed/missing files). - Program-level listener (programListener/processAllComments) walks all comments, processes @story/@req/@supports lines, and reuses a shared cache across the entire file (integration with ESLint lifecycle and caching). - meta.messages defines clear UX messages: - reqMissing: "Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'" - invalidPath: "Invalid story path '{{storyPath}}'",Targeted tests for this story: - tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts (explicitly tagged for this story): - Header: - "* Tests for: docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md" - "* @story docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md" - @req lines mapping directly to REQ-DEEP-PARSE, REQ-DEEP-MATCH, and error-reporting requirements. - Valid cases: - "[REQ-DEEP-PARSE] valid requirement reference existing in story file" uses: ```js // @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md // @req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE ``` Confirms that when the requirement exists in the story file, the rule reports no error. - "[REQ-DEEP-BULLET] valid bullet list requirement existing in bullet story fixture" uses: ```js // @story tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md // @req REQ-BULLET-LIST ``` Combined with tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md, this shows bullet-list formats are handled. - Two valid "[REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS]" cases with @supports and multi-story fixtures (story_multi_a.md, story_multi_b.md) confirm deep validation for @supports across multiple story files. - Invalid cases: - "[REQ-DEEP-MATCH] missing requirement in story file" expects a reqMissing error with data { reqId: "REQ-NON-EXISTENT", storyPath: "docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md" }. - Path safety checks: disallow path traversal and absolute path for @story, both expecting messageId "invalidPath" with the offending storyPath. - Bullet fixture negative case: missing bullet list requirement in story_bullet.md expects reqMissing with correct reqId/storyPath. - @supports negative cases: missing requirement in multi-story fixture and path traversal in supports story path, checking reqMissing and invalidPath respectively. - Jest test run (npm test -- --verbose) shows: - PASS tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts - All valid and invalid scenarios above passed, confirming rule behavior matches expectations for this story.,Fixtures covering different story file structures and formats: - tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md: ```md ## Requirements - REQ-BULLET-LIST - a requirement in bullet list format - REQ-ANOTHER - another requirement ``` - Demonstrates that requirements expressed as bullet list items are correctly discovered by the regex-based parser. - tests/fixtures/story_multi_a.md and story_multi_b.md: - Both contain bullet-list requirements: - story_multi_a.md: REQ-SHARED-ID, REQ-ONLY-A - story_multi_b.md: REQ-SHARED-ID, REQ-ONLY-B - Used by the valid and invalid @supports tests to verify: - Multi-story deep validation. - Requirement IDs scoped per story file (same ID in multiple stories is allowed). - docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md: - Contains requirement identifiers like REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE, which are used in the valid/invalid tests to exercise deep matching in a real story file.,Plugin integration and configuration: - src/index.ts: - RULE_NAMES includes "valid-req-reference" so the rule is dynamically loaded and exported. - TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES maps "traceability/valid-req-reference" to "error". - configs.recommended and configs.strict both include this mapping, so deep validation is part of the standard flat-config presets. - tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts: - Verifies rules object includes "valid-req-reference" in the expected rule list. - Asserts recommended/strict configs contain traceability/valid-req-reference with severity "error" alongside other core rules. - tests/integration/cli-integration.test.ts: - Uses ESLint CLI with the plugin configured and runs rules including: - "traceability/valid-req-reference:error" on code with path traversal and absolute-path @story/@req usage. - Asserts non-zero exit status in those cases, confirming the rule works via the real ESLint CLI, integrated with existing configuration.,User experience and error handling: - src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts: - meta.messages.reqMissing and invalidPath provide clear, specific messages including the missing requirement ID and story path. - loadAndCacheRequirements wraps fs.readFileSync in try/catch and, on error, records an empty Set for that story, preventing rule crashes on malformed or unreadable story files. - validateAndResolveStoryPath rejects path traversal and absolute paths early, reporting invalidPath instead of attempting unsafe filesystem access. - tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts: - Explicitly asserts that both reqMissing and invalidPath are emitted with the correct messageId and data payloads, covering REQ-DEEP-ERROR and dependency story 007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING. - tests/integration/cli-integration.test.ts: - Confirms that when invalid paths are used in annotations, running ESLint with traceability/valid-req-reference causes the CLI to exit with status 1, which is the expected user-facing behavior.,Documentation of behavior and supported formats: - Describes deep validation behavior: - Verifies referenced story files exist and are within the project directory. - Parses story files to extract requirement IDs like REQ-XXX-YYY. - Ensures each @req and each requirement ID after @supports matches extracted IDs in the target story. - Reports invalidPath for traversal/absolute paths and reqMissing for unknown requirements. - Explains requirement ID scoping (only unique within a single story file) and multi-story behavior via @supports. - Provides concrete examples: - Correct use with @story + @req. - Correct multi-story deep validation with @supports. - Incorrect cases for missing requirements, path traversal, and absolute paths. - Explains migration patterns and how valid-req-reference interacts with @story/@req and @supports, satisfying the "Documentation" acceptance criterion.
traceability.notes: Story 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION is fully implemented. The valid-req-reference rule performs deep validation of @req and @supports annotations against actual requirements in story files, using a cached, regex-based parser that works across different markdown structures (plain sections, bullet lists, and multi-story fixtures). Comprehensive unit tests directly tied to this story validate correct and failing scenarios for both requirement existence and path safety, plugin and CLI integration tests confirm the rule is wired into the overall plugin and ESLint usage, and dedicated documentation (docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md) explains the behavior and provides examples. Error handling is graceful (no crashes on unreadable files, clear diagnostic messages for missing requirements and invalid paths). All acceptance criteria and listed requirements for this story are satisfied by concrete code, tests, and documentation in the repository.
